This year's 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade will step off around 8.30 a.m. Eastern Time on Saturday.
The two-day delay was the first on record because of the nor'easter that left tens of thousands without power.
I think the worst scenario could have been you put all this time and effort into something and then you don't get to do it.

He said the students board buses right after their two-and-a-half-mile march on the west side of Manhattan and they go back for classes on Monday.
The Iraqi government is closing border crossings run by Kurdish government forces.
In Paris, Jane Araff reports it's a controversial move to take back control from the Kurdistan region.
Iraqi state media says border forces have closed a crossing with Syria and another with Iran and territory administered by the Kurdish regional government.
Kurds broke away from central government control under Saddam Hussein in 1992 and now administer four majority Kurdish-Iraqi provinces, including border operations.
Earlier this week, the Iraqi prime minister announced that the federal oil ministry would now run some of the biggest oil fields that are currently managed by Iraq's Kurdistan regional government.
The government accuses Kurds of diverting oil proceeds. They deny it.
The Kurdish leadership says it will not give up control of its borders or the oil fields.
Jane Araff, NPR News, Amman.
Kurdish leaders have rejected Baghdad's moves as unilateral, sparking protests in Erbil.
The UN has urged both sides to use constitutional channels instead.
Stocks rose as this holiday shortened week ended early.
These gains were welcomed by investors who have spent the past several days worrying about A.I., and PR's Maham Javed reports.
After several days of volatile fluctuations, mostly due to tech indexes,
U.S. stocks posted strong returns this week before the market closed today.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.6 percent with broad gains.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 1.2 percent.
And the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite rose 2.3 percent.
The biggest jump this week was on Monday when Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, was reinstated as the head of the semiconductor company.
Those gains have held despite big ups and downs on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Semiconductor stocks bounced back as investors relaxed about instability in the A.I. market.
The market was shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday and closed early for Black Friday.
Maham Javed, NPR News.
And this is NPR from Culver City, California.
Airbnb is taking a closer look at what hosts ask guests to do before they check out.
The company has started reviewing listings under a new house rules policy that took effect last week.
And PR's Michaela Gray reports guests have been sharing some of the more demanding checkout instructions on social media.
Taylor Renfro, a social media travel influencer, has contributed to the online discourse against strict hosts.
She says she's experienced unreasonable cleaning expectations before the policy change and has moved towards staying in hotels instead.
You don't have to worry about any of those cleaning things.
And most of the time you get a continental breakfast and people come in and clean your room every morning.
So it's like it is a better deal.
The new policy says house rules should be reasonable.
For example, hosts can ask guests to put used dishes in the sink, but shouldn't ask them to wash or put them away.
Airbnb says it'll now be looking at listings and emailing hosts if their house rules appear to be violating the new policy.
Michaela Gray, NPR News.
There's about two hours left before polls close on the island of Taiwan in closely watched local elections by both Beijing and Washington,
including the Taipei City mayoral race.
Puma Shen, of the rival Democratic Progressive Party, is challenging the incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT or Kuomintang Party,
which has traditionally been the stronghold of Taipei.
More than 19 million voters are eligible to vote across 22 cities and counties.
The four-year appointments signaled political shifts ahead of the 2028 presidential race.
